rationale: The quote only says a "self-checking data system" was undeveloped; it names no prediction of elections or behavior, so it points loosely at statistical forecasting.
Rohorses are commanded by thought ("encephalopathed"), matching thought control of a machine, but the quote gives no mechanism and the real milestone is only a cursor.
Robot bartenders serving and mixing drinks match a robot serving patrons, as at the 1985 robot restaurant; the intoxication-judging by speech is far beyond that waiter.
A stereo projection map in the flagship's Information Center is a 3D display for planning, like the volumetric planning display, but stereo projection on a flat wall differs from a volumetric image.
Photographing retinas for blood-vessel patterns is exactly retinal-pattern biometrics as in the 1984 scanner; it predates by decades but the context (impersonation vs access control) differs.
A machine that hears questions and answers from a huge memory matches question answering by computer, but the quote names no language processing and the answers come from tapes.
Only mentions "the sleep-learner" as a known device in passing, giving no detail of how it teaches, so it is only evocative of sleep-learning experiments.
A part-organic artificial brain gestures toward biological computing, but Adleman's DNA test-tube calculation is a different thing from an organic thinking brain.
Waking enveloped in darkness inside a spacesuit suggests a convincingly real simulated world, but the quote does not state the machine or its senses-feeding mechanism.
Appliances doing tasks "at your mental command" match controlling devices by thought, but the energy-finger mechanism is invented and the real milestone is a cursor.
Doors released by a specific combination of thought waves match brain-signal control of a machine; the real 1998 implant only moved a cursor, and thought-wave authentication is a different use.
A humanoid automaton reacting with gestures to certain sounds is a crude sound-triggered device, not recognition of words and commands as in the VIP-100.
A typist speaks into a microphone and her typing machine transcribes the words as type, matching voice-to-text dictation; the human intermediary and tape differ from Voicerad.
An abstract concept "hurled into the machine" makes it find a recording, matching thought-operated machinery in function; no neural-signal mechanism is given.
A machine reads a mind and shows the thoughts as images, matching the 2006 fMRI reconstruction of imagined visual patterns in function, though the real result was only simple patterns.
A computer synthesizing a story outline from existing books is automatic text composition, loosely akin to FoG's generating forecasts, but source and output type differ.
A belt gadget reading thoughts word for word far exceeds the 2006 decoding of simple imagined visual patterns; the direction is right but the capability differs.
A door opening on a whistled code word is sound-command operation, matching voice-operated control in function, but a whistle is not recognized speech.
The quote only says scanning and decision elements tripled a device's mass; it hints at a thinking personal gadget but says nothing of notes, reminders or pocket size.
A lenticular tank showing every unit of the enemy in exact detail is a 3D tactical display like volumetric display, though the quote gives no mechanism or viewing from all sides.
Hiding a capable brain in subminiaturized circuits matches miniaturized solid-state electronics in function; "semipsionic" is invented and the integrated-circuit milestone is a general one.
A robot monster moving on its operator's mental directions matches thought control of a machine; the quote gives no neural interface mechanism beyond "picked up".
A brain recorder feeding a device that projects a 3D picture of thoughts matches displaying mental images, but the real 2006 work reconstructed only simple flat patterns.
The quotation says only that the Brain is involved; it has nothing about casting or counting votes.
City-wide calls for electrograph and viewplate records on any subject match remote retrieval from a central store, though the 1967 telephone terminal retrieved text citations, not images.
Watching dots in a tri-di display is a three-dimensional tracking display in function, but the quote offers no volumetric mechanism.
A Brain actuated by the wearer's thoughts via headset matches thought-controlled machinery, but the lethal-effector context and nonexistent mechanism differ from the cursor implant.
Cars reading magnetic tags and transmitting to a central records office is automated identity checking, only loosely related to ankle transmitters reporting an offender's location.
A small ship-board computer figuring orbital and blast data in flight matches the Gemini onboard computer's navigation function and mechanism; the context differs.
A machine converting a mind's readings into visible shapes matches thought display in function, but the 2006 decoding was only simple imagined patterns.
An automatic computer on the boat computing distance, velocity and landing time is an onboard navigation computer like Gemini's; the landing context differs.
A lawnmower machine that stops at an obstruction and resumes its path matches an autonomous mower's function, though the 1969 MowBot's actual obstacle handling is not shown.
Electronic brains joined to neural paths evoke neural implants, but a cochlear implant restoring hearing is a very different use from an implanted computer.
A self-activating, problem-seeking computer with senses and actuators matches a machine doing science on its own, but Adam's hypothesis-testing is narrower and the quote shows no experiments.
A galvanometer-based psychometer used to extract truth from patients matches measuring physiological signals for lie detection; the 1921 polygraph used blood pressure and breathing.
A lab-built human double that stands in for the original matches a robot copy of a person, but Disney's Lincoln was a stage show figure, not indistinguishable.
Electrodes on subvocal nerve impulses fed to a translator that outputs words is a thought-to-speech interface, not the text-to-speech synthesis of the Kurzweil reader.
The quote says only that Rip had plotted orbits before but never for real use; the computer is not mentioned, so it is only loosely about orbit computation.
A machine scanning stored scientific knowledge of a million planets is mass retrieval; the quote shows no hypothesis forming or experiments, unlike Adam.
Seeing a simulated war with full visual and auditory hallucinations instead of printouts matches experiencing a computer simulation in immersive form, but no head display or mechanism is given.
Eye-reflection tracking triggering a spoken word of the scrolled text matches a machine voicing written words, though the 1976 Kurzweil reader used a scanner for the blind, not eye tracking.
Only a character remarking a hallucination felt real; it conveys the realism of a simulation but no machine, display or interaction.
A cap whose wearer's thoughts are poured onto a screen via a lens matches showing thoughts as images; the lens-projection mechanism is nothing like fMRI decoding.
Summoning a mess-robot that serves dishes matches a robot serving diners, as in the Pasadena robot restaurant, though ordering and delivery details are missing.
The quote says only that a robot responds to an auditory mechanism like an electric eye, which suggests sound triggering but not recognizing spoken words.
Dream-machine tapes taken at night to be ready for a job next day imply machine-delivered instruction during sleep, matching sleep learning in function, with no mechanism stated.
Sorting people to levels by machines that sense their wrist-bands of rank is automatic identification by a worn token, akin to card-based access, but the 1961 system recorded attendance.
Passing a card before a robot's scanner and getting a click of acknowledgement is machine-read ID checking, but the milestone is a patrolling security robot, not a card reader.
Mechanisms that react selectively to electrical impulses of brain cells state the core brain-signal-to-machine mechanism; the use and context are unspecified.
A machine reading a data tape and ruling on a plea is automated judging, whereas LEXIS was a research service for lawyers, so only loosely related.
The quote only has characters taking language lessons en route; hypnotic or sleeping instruction is not stated.
An electric signal at each seat to register votes matches electrical vote counting in function, but the 1964 milestone used punched cards tallied by computer.
A registration robot handling routine cases and passing odd ones to a manager is an automated desk clerk, loosely like robot waiters in a restaurant.
Pictures identified with an ident-card at police headquarters are matched by card, not by automated face matching, so it only points toward face-based identification.
A memory-prober reading a man's whole life history goes far beyond the 2006 decoding of simple imagined visual patterns, matching only in aspiration.
A computer failing to account for the lunar rocket's reduced mass shows computers doing flight calculations for lunar maneuvers, matching onboard navigation in function; details are thin.
A camp computer radio-controlling robots as their brain matches a central computer directing a fleet, as with Volvo's computer-guided carriers; context and guidance method differ.
Computers compensating course and power in real time to keep a ship from breaking up is automated flight guidance in function, but the gravitic setting is fictional.
Translating brain waves into pictures matches thought display in function; the claimed mechanism is just reading waves and the 2006 result was only simple patterns.
A cap that shows a visualized world on a screen and carries the user in matches entering a computer-generated world, but the brain-cap interface and transport are invented.
An automated factory that produces and repairs robots with no supervision matches Fanuc's lights-out robot-building plant; the atomic power source and indefinite lifespan differ.
A film adding taste, smell and touch so you are in the story and the shadows reply matches interactive multisensory VR in function and aim; no headset or tracking is described.
Punching a designation on a keyboard and seeing the record on a screen matches terminal-based retrieval, but 1967 results were bibliographic text over a phone link.
Books that reply to queries with locations in a library match question answering in function, but START answered public questions in text on the internet.
Detecting minute brain discharges with a machine to read thoughts matches decoding brain activity in function, but fMRI decoding recovered only simple imagined images.
A three-dimensional map hanging in the air matches a 3D display viewable from all sides, but the Perspecta was an enclosed volumetric dome used for medical planning.
A machine that turns thoughts into spoken words is far more than the 2006 reconstruction of simple visual patterns; it matches only in direction.
A device projecting a three-dimensional picture into a dark viewing space is a 3D display like volumetric display, though the quote includes no volumetric mechanism or use.
Brushing a hand across a screen to switch machinery on and off matches a touch-sensitive panel input, as in PLATO IV; the control-of-machinery context differs.
Two bright flashes from a small tube held to the eyes evoke an eye scan for identification, though the quote does not say the pattern is read for identity.
A camera feeding a police computer that compares a description to files matches automated face matching in function, but the quote involves a description, not stored images.
A menu appearing on a screen that rises from the table when a diner sits is an electronic display screen, but the quote gives no computing or graphics mechanism like Whirlwind's CRT.
A street robot holding your voice pattern and acting on it matches speaker recognition by stored voiceprint; the relay-message context differs from computer-center access control.
An animated mannequin figure carrying a vase-like vessel hints at a serving android, but the quote shows no serving of patrons.
A huge tank filled with crawling lights for fleet units is a large 3D tactical display, but its scale and lack of a depth-rendering mechanism differ from the volumetric medical display.
Hypnotic instruction by day continuing through the night's sleep matches teaching during sleep in function, but no device or mechanism is given.
A flickering, swarming-light image filling out a complete 3D form in the cabin is a volumetric-style display in function, but the quote does not say it is viewable from any side or used for planning.
Saying the single word "first" to an elevator that then acts is a spoken isolated-word command, close to the VIP-100's recognition; the elevator setting differs from industrial terminals.
A calculating machine forecasting the results of any act is a general consequence predictor; it matches a broadcast election forecast only in a very loose way.
Saying "Open" to a lock that recognizes the speaker and admits him matches voice-command recognition plus speaker check; it is a door use rather than data entry.
A mechanical cortex of ninety billion electronic cells matches a brain-inspired network of many simple units in function, but no learning is stated and LeNet was a digit reader.
Being thrust into the picture and having to solve the situation describes a lived simulated environment, matching immersive VR in function, though no display device is named.
A robowaiter approaching with a menu board in its metal hands matches robot waiters taking orders as at the Pasadena robot restaurant; the context is similar, details of ordering absent.
A wall scanner checking people against a large store of registered images and data to admit them matches face-recognition access control; the era's database and scale differ.
Cubes ruled by will through telepathy match thought control of machines, but there is no neural-signal mechanism and the real milestone was a cursor.
Portable mass-production factories turning out a complete ship every eleven seconds are fully automated production, but Fanuc's plant builds robots, with no raw-material mining or transmutation.
A pocket disk held to the left eye for twenty seconds to record an eyeprint is retinal biometric capture used as signature; the portable metal-disk form differs from the 1984 scanner.
Temple contact-buttons feeding a machine that writes a secretary's thoughts match thought transcription in function, but the 2006 fMRI work decoded only simple images.
Instruments built as robots that play themselves point toward machines performing music, a loose link to CSIRAC playing tunes, with no composing or computing in the quote.
The explanation that the subject is thrust into the scenario rather than viewing a picture matches an immersive simulation, but no machine or interface is described.
A huge three-dimensional chart of a star system in the room's center is a 3D map display like volumetric display, but the quote has no mechanism or multi-angle viewing.
A thumb pressed on a doorplate's electronic grid to open the door is fingerprint recognition at an entrance, but the milestone is computerized fingerprint analysis for identification.
A robot merely stating that it gives information is a very thin hint of an information attendant robot, with no setting or interaction described.
Conceiving a means for the spoken word to be directly translatable into print states the dictation-transcription function but gives no mechanism.
Speaking a demand for a statistical summary into a mouthpiece and getting it printed within a moment matches remote computer retrieval in function; the voice input goes beyond the 1967 terminal.
A servo-robot waiter seating diners at a table matches a robot serving patrons in a restaurant, but taking orders and serving food are not shown.
Feeding all the variations of the French opening from books into the Machine's memory describes a stored opening book in a chess machine, but the 1977 commercial product was a small consumer unit.
An infrared scanner showing temperature as colored spots is thermal imaging for a pilot, not the interpretation of camera images by a machine as in Roberts' thesis.
A machine that throws captives' thoughts upon a screen matches displaying thoughts in function; the hypnosis-driven mechanism differs from fMRI decoding.
"Ear-tubes" that respond to sound as a computer input channel point at voice input in function, with no recognition mechanism or vocabulary stated.
A ship with its computer brain built in as an intrinsic part says nothing of calculating courses or orbits, and only loosely suggests a ship-integrated computer.

A calculator clicking out course results to six decimals while gyroscopes lock the ship's orientation matches onboard navigation computing and attitude control in function, with no automation of burns described.
Fitting the eye into a cup at a wall, with retinal patterns noted as non-duplicable, matches retinal-scan access control in function, mechanism and context, as in the 1984 EyeDentify.
The quote only describes a keyless typewriter-shaped machine on a desk; the speech recording it is meant to perform is not in the text, so it points loosely at dictation machines.

A machine returning a song in English in a conditioned person's voice produces speech from a voice model, matching synthesized speech in function, but translation and voice cloning far exceed the 1976 reading machine.
Recorded words electronically put together to answer questions is assembled-speech output, matching speech synthesis in function, while the Kurzweil machine synthesized speech from print by rule.
Thoughts hurled against the computer's psychocoil to get an answer match thought-driven computer operation, but there is no signal-reading mechanism and the milestone only moved a cursor.
A photoelectric tracer searching a file for anyone resembling a description is a rough image search, with no face matching stated, so only evocative of face recognition.
The remark that machines run the machines hints at self-maintaining automation but is a single aside with no detail on factory operations.
The quote has only a character producing the "mechanical educator" before a creature; what it does is not stated, so it connects to mind reading only by the label.

Dropping a plastic disk into a slot so the machine reads and responds matches inserting an ID card into a reader that identifies the holder; the voice announcement differs from the attendance recording.
The quote only has a speaker threatening to blast rows of machines; it says nothing about data analysis or tracking people.
Devices delicate enough to detect the brain's rho waves match brain-signal detection for reading thought, but the quote gives only detection with no decoding of content.
A compartmented machine of synonym sets for composing prose evokes mechanical text generation, a loose link to FoG's data-driven forecasts.

A helmet that detects the brain's motor impulses and radios them to guide a robot states the key mechanism of reading motor-cortex signals to control a machine; the whole-body robot context far exceeds a cursor.

A tone generator spanning the audio range and rapidly controlled by the machine in pitch and volume describes electronically generated voice sounds, matching speech synthesis in function with a different mechanism from the Votrax reader.
An implanted device sensing a nervous-tract change and signaling a transceiver matches an implant reading neural activity to operate a machine; the teleport use is fictional.
A man plugging in a machine and playing a reel of his father's voice shows recorded-audio playback, but nothing says it teaches a sleeper.
Automatic power machinery needing only a handful of attendants suggests unattended operation, but it is one plant component and not a factory producing goods.
Feeding a coded description into a file search for any person resembling it is automated record retrieval in function; the photoelectric tracer is far from a bibliographic terminal.
A thumb in the door's whorl-lock to enter a cabin is fingerprint-keyed access, but the milestone concerns computer analysis of prints for matching.
Teaching arbitrary knowledge to a subject asleep matches sleep learning in function; the 2019 result only formed simple word associations.
The quote describes egg-shaped treaded robots with jointed arms and says nothing of hearing or obeying spoken orders.
The servo-tracer merely "went to sleep"; the quote gives no sign of tracking a person's location.
Mathematically-exact translation of oral sound into script anticipates speech transcription and spelling reform, matching function but with no mechanism beyond the phrase.
Working machines by sheer will without hands matches thought control in function, but the quote is only a speculation with no neural mechanism.
Collecting thought as electric current directly from the thinker's brain matches reading brain signals, but the quote does not decode content as the 2006 work did.
Touching numbered knobs wired to the kitchen to order dinner is an electric ordering panel, only loosely like touch input on a screen.
Reading the Fenachrone plans from their brains with a mechanical educator is full-content mind reading, far beyond the 2006 decoding of simple imagined patterns.
Islands acting as caretakers that keep a field spruced evoke self-maintaining automation, but it is far from a factory or plant.
Talking at the Speak-a-Type while its keys rattle to keep up is a speech-driven typewriter, matching voice dictation transcription in function and mechanism; speed and vocabulary are idealized.
Hiring a computer and feeding libraries into its memory to solve problems hints at rented computing and large stores, but retrieval of matching records is not described.
An apparatus responding to his thoughts from a distance matches thought control of a device, with no mechanism and the 1998 milestone being implanted cursor control.
Reading a dead officer's ideas from his brain is open-ended mind reading, only evocative of the 2006 decoding of imagined patterns.
The quote is about physical sabotage burning out a calculator wing, which is not computer intrusion over a network.
Cars recording buyers' statistics and correlating the data loosely resemble computerized rating of consumers, but credit scoring used loan application data, not physical measurements.
Data fed into the Elecalc to determine drive time, angle and velocity is a computer used to compute flight settings, but it is not stated whether it controls the maneuver.
A little machine picking up control-room orders and adjusting every machine below matches centrally directed plant automation in function, but Fanuc's plant is robot-built and lights-out.
A cap said to read all thoughts and prevent lying is open-ended mind reading, matching the 2006 fMRI decoding only in direction.
A poetry machine that "emits" something is a bare mention of machine-made verse, loosely related to automated text generation.
A planet's surface springing on a shipboard screen in three-dimensional reality is a 3D display in function, but a screen differs from a viewable-from-all-sides volumetric display.
Sound analyzers that the living voice cannot be imitated past describe automatic voice authentication of speakers; the military command context differs from computer-center access.
A station packed with robotic equipment that is self-sustaining once set matches unattended automated operation, with no production or factory function stated.
An idealizator that makes thoughts visible by converting psychons to light matches displaying thoughts in function; the physics mechanism is invented.
A quick computation on the planetary calculator followed by firing steering rockets matches a computer used to plan a course, but the human relays the result to the engines.
Thinking "speed" and the body responding evokes thought control, but it is a brain housed in the robot body, not a signal link to an external machine.
A Giant Brain oracle that students can question matches question answering by computer in function; the quote gives no language mechanism and START answers from a web database.
A test pit in which you have no doubt you are a colonist responding to stimuli as if on the planet matches an immersive simulated reality, but no device or display is described.
A citizen's plate in the slot recording the vote with the Brain's tally matches machine-recorded and counted votes, while the 1964 counties used punched cards for computer tallying.
A body-worn device that tells a worker what to do instant to instant matches a carried information aid, but a Psion Organiser is a pocket database with no real-time instructions.
